name: @kitora/windows
description: Kitora's floating window manager: a framework-free core (states, snapping, z-order, persistence) with DOM gestures, React bindings and macOS / Windows / neutral chrome presets.

exports.name: isMember
exports.description: Narrows a string to a member of a closed set (parsing persisted layouts, data attributes).
exports.signature: <const T extends string>(set: readonly T[], value: string) => value is T

exports.name: WINDOW_STATES
exports.description:
Where a window is in its lifecycle (W17). Ordered by restore rank: `restore`
walks back down this order through the window's restore stack (states.ts),
which is what makes maximised → minimised → restore → restore land on
maximised, then normal (W27).

exports.name: WindowState
exports.description: A window lifecycle state, one of `WINDOW_STATES`.

exports.name: STATE_RANK
exports.description: The rank of each state in the restore stack; ranks strictly increase from bottom to top.

exports.name: WINDOW_TIERS
exports.description:
Paint tier, applied above the activation order (W56, W57): `below` for desktop
widgets, `above` for inspectors and pickers. An owned window paints at least
at its owner's tier, so a palette of an always-on-top window stays on top.

exports.name: WindowTier
exports.description: A paint tier, one of `WINDOW_TIERS`.

exports.name: TIER_RANK
exports.description: Paint rank per tier; a higher rank paints above every window of a lower one.

exports.name: RESIZE_EDGES
exports.description: The eight resize grips (W6): compass names, so `includes("w")` reads as "touches the west edge".

exports.name: ResizeEdge
exports.description: A resize grip, one of `RESIZE_EDGES`.

exports.name: KEEP_POLICIES
KeepPolicy
exports.description: How much of a window must stay in the work area, one of `KEEP_POLICIES`.

exports.name: TILE_MODES
exports.description: Tile arrangements (W71): a near-square grid, side by side, or stacked.

exports.name: TileMode
exports.description: A tile arrangement, one of `TILE_MODES`.

exports.name: DOUBLE_CLICK_ACTIONS
exports.description: What a title-bar double-click does (W22): macOS lets the user choose between the first two. Read by the dom layer.

exports.name: DoubleClickAction
exports.description: What a title-bar double-click does, one of `DOUBLE_CLICK_ACTIONS`.

exports.name: WINDOW_EVENT_TYPES
exports.description:
Lifecycle events a manager emits (W132). `order` = the paint order changed; `flags` = collapsed, hidden or
attention changed; `mode` = a keyboard move or size mode started, committed or was cancelled (W88, W89).

exports.name: WindowEventType
exports.description: A manager lifecycle event type, one of `WINDOW_EVENT_TYPES`.

exports.name: MAXIMIZE_TARGET
exports.description: The snap target that maximises instead of filling a zone (the top edge, W34). Not a zone id, so a zone set cannot shadow it.

exports.name: TEXT_DIRECTIONS
exports.description:
Reading direction of a desktop (W108). `rtl` cascades new windows from the
top-right; snap zone ids stay physical (`left` is the screen's left), and the
ui layer mirrors the title-bar controls through CSS logical order.

exports.name: TextDirection
exports.description: A desktop reading direction, one of `TEXT_DIRECTIONS`.

exports.name: WINDOW_MODALITIES
exports.description:
Modality (W58, W59). `none`: an ordinary modeless window. `app`: blocks every
window outside its own owned subtree until it closes (an app-modal dialog).
`owner`: window-modal, blocks its owner only (a sheet on a document window);
without an owner it behaves as `app`. Blocked windows cannot be focused (focus goes to
the blocker), moved or resized; the bindings make them inert.

exports.name: WindowModality
exports.description: A window modality, one of `WINDOW_MODALITIES`.

exports.name: KEYBOARD_MODES
exports.description: Keyboard gestures (W88, W89): Windows' system-menu Move and Size, GNOME and KDE Alt+F7 and Alt+F8.

exports.name: KeyboardMode
exports.description: A keyboard gesture, one of `KEYBOARD_MODES`: move or size.

exports.name: KEYBOARD_MODE_PHASES
exports.description: How a keyboard mode event ends up: it started, was committed (Enter, a click, focus moving on) or cancelled (Escape restores the start).

exports.name: KeyboardModePhase
exports.description: How a keyboard mode event ends up, one of `KEYBOARD_MODE_PHASES`.

exports.name: KEYBOARD_REGION_ATTR
exports.description:
The keyboard kit's region attribute (K69, its `REGION_ATTR`). Every window
and the taskbar carry it, so F6 / Shift+F6 cycle through them when the host
installs the keyboard kit's region navigation (W98). A plain string here, not
an import, so no layer but `keyboard` depends on the keyboard kit; the plugin
test pins it to the kit's own constant.

exports.name: TASKBAR_REGION
exports.description: The taskbar's region name: what `window.focusTaskbar` and F6 navigation look for.

exports.name: rightOf
exports.description: The right edge of `r`.

exports.name: bottomOf
exports.description: The bottom edge of `r`.

exports.name: clamp
exports.description: `value` limited to `[lo, hi]`; when the range is empty (`hi < lo`), `lo` wins, so a minimum is never broken by a maximum.
exports.signature: (value: number, lo: number, hi: number) => number

exports.name: translateRect
exports.description: `r` moved by `d`.

exports.name: insetRect
exports.description: `r` shrunk by `insets`; a side never goes negative, so an over-inset desktop is an empty rect, not an inverted one.

exports.name: sameRect
exports.description: True when both rects have the same four numbers (events fire only on a real change).

exports.name: Point
exports.description: A point or a 2D offset.

exports.name: Rect
exports.description: An axis-aligned box, `DOMRect`-compatible on the four fields the core reads.

exports.name: Size
exports.description: A width and a height.

exports.name: Insets
exports.description: Space reserved at each side of the desktop (a taskbar, a dock, a header), W48.

exports.name: NO_INSETS
exports.description: No reserved space.

exports.name: HALF
exports.description: Half, for centres; named so the maths reads as intent.

exports.name: sizeBounds
exports.description: The four numeric bounds of `limits`, with the minimum clamped to the maximum (a max smaller than a min wins).
exports.signature: (limits: SizeLimits) => { readonly minW: number; readonly maxW: number; readonly minH: number; readonly maxH: number; }

exports.name: clampSize
exports.description: `size` inside `limits`.

exports.name: constrainPosition
exports.description:
`rect` moved (never resized) so `keep` holds against `area` (W45). `full`: the
whole rect inside, pinned to the top-left when it is larger than the area;
`title`: the top edge between the area's top and its bottom minus a title
bar, and at least `minVisible` px of width inside horizontally.
exports.signature: (rect: Rect, area: Rect, options: KeepOptions) => Rect

exports.name: fitIntoArea
exports.description:
`rect` made to fit `area` after the desktop shrank or a saved layout came from
a bigger screen (W47, W83): each side larger than the area shrinks to it (not
below the window's minimum), then the position is constrained by `keep`.
exports.signature: (rect: Rect, area: Rect, limits: SizeLimits, options: KeepOptions) => Rect

exports.name: quantize
exports.description: `value` rounded to the nearest multiple of `step` counted from `origin`; a step ≤ 0 leaves it alone (W11).
exports.signature: (value: number, step: number, origin: number) => number

exports.name: snapRectToGrid
exports.description: The rect with its top-left on the grid (W11, W31).
exports.signature: (rect: Rect, step: number, origin: Point) => Rect

exports.name: resizeRect
exports.description:
The rect after dragging `edge` by `delta` from `start` (W6, W8–W11). The edge
opposite the grip stays put (or the centre, with `fromCenter`); a side-edge
resize under an aspect lock changes the other dimension from the top or left.
Every limit holds at once: min, max, the area and the aspect ratio; when they
cannot all hold, the minimum wins (a window never shrinks below it).
exports.signature: (start: Rect, edge: ResizeEdge, delta: Point, options: ResizeOptions) => Rect

exports.name: magnetLines
exports.description:
The lines `rect` may cling to: the area's four edges, and the edges of every
other window that overlaps it on the other axis (within `threshold`), so a
window snaps beside a neighbour, not to a window far above it — macOS's rule.
exports.signature: (rect: Rect, area: Rect, others: readonly Rect[], threshold: number) => MagnetLines

exports.name: magnetize
exports.description: `rect` shifted so its nearest edge on each axis sits on a magnet line within `threshold` px (W29, W30).
exports.signature: (rect: Rect, lines: MagnetLines, threshold: number) => Rect

exports.name: restoreUnderPointer
exports.description:
Where a maximised or snapped window lands when the user drags it away (W23,
W41): back to its normal `size`, placed so the pointer keeps the same relative
x on the title bar and the same distance below the top edge (capped to the
window's height), the way both operating systems do it.
exports.signature: (from: Rect, size: Size, pointer: Point) => Rect

exports.name: SizeLimits
exports.description: Size limits of one window (W8). `max: null` = only the work area limits it.

exports.name: AspectLock
exports.description:
Aspect-ratio lock (W9). `ratio` is content width / content height; `extra` is
fixed chrome around the content (a title bar's height), so a 16:9 video keeps
16:9 inside a window whose frame is 32 px taller — react-rnd's
`lockAspectRatioExtraHeight`, generalised to both axes.

exports.name: DEFAULT_MIN_SIZE
exports.description: Room for a title, its controls and a line of content; what a window gets when it names no minimum.

exports.name: DEFAULT_TITLE_HEIGHT
exports.description: Height of the title bar the `title` keep policy keeps reachable and a collapsed window shows (W24, W45).

exports.name: DEFAULT_MIN_VISIBLE
exports.description: Width of a window that must stay inside the work area under the `title` policy, so its title can still be grabbed.

exports.name: KeepOptions
exports.description: What `constrainPosition` needs besides the rect.

exports.name: ResizeOptions
exports.description: Options for `resizeRect`.

exports.name: MagnetLines
exports.description: Lines a moving window's edges cling to (W29, W30): x positions for its left/right edges, y for its top/bottom.

exports.name: findZone
exports.description: The zone named `id`, or null.
exports.signature: (zones: readonly SnapZone[], id: string) => SnapZone | null

exports.name: zoneRect
exports.description: A zone's rect in pixels inside `area`, rounded so neighbouring zones share an edge exactly.

exports.name: resolveSnapTarget
exports.description:
The snap target for a drag whose pointer is at `pointer` (W32–W34). Near a
side, the corner bands decide between the half and the quarter (W33 wins
inside `corner` px of a corner); a pointer past the edge (outside the area)
counts as on it. A target naming a zone missing from `zones` is no target.
exports.signature: (pointer: Point, area: Rect, options: SnapOptions) => SnapTarget | null

exports.name: FractionRect
exports.description: A rect as fractions (0–1) of the work area.

exports.name: SnapZone
exports.description: One snap zone. `id` is what `snap(id, zone)` and saved layouts name.

exports.name: DEFAULT_SNAP_ZONES
exports.description: The built-in zones: halves, quarters, thirds and two-thirds (W32, W33, W35).

exports.name: SnapLayout
exports.description: A snap layout: zones shown together in the snap layouts menu (W36).

exports.name: DEFAULT_SNAP_LAYOUTS
exports.description: The Windows 11 menu's layouts, as data over `DEFAULT_SNAP_ZONES`.

exports.name: EdgeTargets
exports.description: Where each edge and corner of the work area sends a drag: a zone id, `"maximize"`, or null for nothing.

exports.name: DEFAULT_EDGE_TARGETS
exports.description: The OS mapping: sides to halves, corners to quarters, the top edge maximises, the bottom edge does nothing.

exports.name: SnapOptions
exports.description: Snapping options (W43).

exports.name: DEFAULT_SNAP_OPTIONS
exports.description: Defaults close to Windows 11: a pointer touching the edge, a generous corner, a light magnet.

exports.name: SnapTarget
exports.description: What a drag would do on release.

exports.name: canEnter
exports.description:
True when a window with `caps` may enter `target`. Snapping resizes, so it
needs `resizable`; maximise and fullscreen need `maximizable`; minimise needs
`minimizable`. Entering the state it is already in is not a transition.
exports.signature: (current: WindowState, target: EnterableState, caps: WindowCapabilities) => boolean

exports.name: enterState
exports.description: `core` after entering `target` (the caller checked `canEnter`). Snapped → snapped keeps the stack (a different zone).

exports.name: restoreState
exports.description: `core` after one `restore`: the top of the restore stack, else `normal`; null when already normal (nothing to do).

exports.name: StateCore
exports.description: A window's state and its restore stack (bottom first).

exports.name: NORMAL_STATE
exports.description: The state every window starts in, with nothing to restore.

exports.name: EnterableState
exports.description: A state other than `normal`: the ones a window enters; `normal` is reached by `restore` or by moving it.

exports.name: WindowCapabilities
exports.description: What a window allows (W12, W17): the manager checks these before any transition.

exports.name: ALL_CAPABILITIES
exports.description: Everything allowed: the default for a window that names no capabilities.

exports.name: rootOf
exports.description: The top-level window of `id`'s owner chain (itself when it has no owner). A missing or cyclic owner ends the walk.

exports.name: isOwnedBy
exports.description: True when `ancestor` is on `id`'s owner chain (not `id` itself).
exports.signature: (id: string, ancestor: string, nodes: ZNodes) => boolean

exports.name: subtreeOf
exports.description: `id` and every window it owns, directly or not, in `stack` order.
exports.signature: (id: string, stack: readonly string[], nodes: ZNodes) => string[]

exports.name: raise
exports.description:
The stack with `id` raised (rule 1): its owner group moves to the top, and
inside the group `id` with its own subtree goes last, so the window and the
palettes it owns paint above its owner and its siblings.
exports.signature: (stack: readonly string[], id: string, nodes: ZNodes) => string[]

exports.name: effectiveTier
exports.description: The highest tier on `id`'s owner chain, itself included (rule 2).

exports.name: paintOrder
exports.description: Paint order, bottom first: the activation stack stably sorted by effective tier (rule 2).

exports.name: ZNode
exports.description: What the z-order needs to know about one window.

exports.name: MODAL_RANK
exports.description: The paint rank of an app-modal window and its owned windows: above the `above` tier, so nothing it blocks can cover it.

exports.name: ZNodes
exports.description: The windows by id, for owner lookups.

exports.name: cascadeRect
exports.description:
The rect of the `index`-th cascaded window of `size` in `area`. Slots run
diagonally from the area's top-left (top-right when `direction` is `rtl`,
W108) and wrap to the first slot when the next one would leave the area, so
a long cascade never walks off the desktop.
exports.signature: (index: number, size: Size, area: Rect, step?: number, direction?: TextDirection) => Rect

exports.name: tileRects
exports.signature: (count: number, area: Rect, mode: TileMode) => Rect[]

exports.name: CASCADE_STEP
exports.description: Offset between cascaded windows: one title bar, so each title stays visible.

exports.name: parseLayout
exports.description:
`value` as a layout, or every reason it is not one (W82). Checks the version,
every window field, duplicate ids, and that `stack`, `mru` and `focused` are
strings; ids they name that no saved window has are dropped later by
`applyLayout`, not rejected here, so an edited layout still loads.

exports.name: createMemoryLayoutStore
exports.description:
The default store: memory only, gone on reload. Values are kept as JSON text,
so a saved layout cannot be changed through a reference the caller kept, and
a round trip behaves like the `localStorage` store's.

exports.name: LAYOUT_VERSION
exports.description: The layout format this code writes and reads. A different version is rejected, never guessed at.

exports.name: SavedWindow
exports.description: One window as saved. `rect` is the normal rect; the state and zone say what is shown.

exports.name: Layout
exports.description: A whole desktop as saved (W81). `stack` is the activation order bottom first; `mru` most recent first.

exports.name: ParseLayoutResult
exports.description: `parseLayout`'s answer: the layout, or every reason it was rejected.

exports.name: LayoutStore
exports.description:
Where layouts live (W84, W86). Keyed by name, so a host keeps several named
layouts. `load` returns the raw stored value: callers run it through
`parseLayout`, because a store holds whatever an older version wrote.

exports.name: createWindowManager
exports.description: Creates one manager for one desktop.

exports.name: DEFAULT_WINDOW_SIZE
exports.description: A new window's size when the host names none.

exports.name: WindowManagerOptions
exports.description: Construction options. Only `bounds` is required: everything else has a documented default.

exports.name: WindowSpec
exports.description: What `open` takes. Only `title` and `data` are required.

exports.name: WindowGuard
exports.description: Vetoes (W17, W25). `beforeClose` may be async (an "unsaved changes" confirm); `beforeState` is sync, since gestures commit synchronously.

exports.name: WindowFlags
exports.description: Flags orthogonal to the state (W24, W26, W80).

exports.name: WindowSnapshot
exports.description: One window as the outside world sees it: an immutable snapshot.

exports.name: KeyboardModeState
exports.description: A keyboard move or size mode in progress (W88, W89): arrows step it, Enter commits, Escape restores the start.

props.name: id
props.description: Id of the window being moved or sized.

props.name: kind
props.description: Which gesture is running: `move` or `size`.

exports.name: DesktopSnapshot
exports.description: The whole desktop. `windows` in open order; `order` = paint order bottom first; `mru` most recent first.

exports.name: WindowEvent
exports.description: Lifecycle events (W132).

exports.name: MovePreview
exports.description: A move preview (W37): nothing is committed until `commit` (invariant 3).

exports.name: MoveUpdateOptions
exports.description: Per-update options of a move.

exports.name: MoveGesture
exports.description: A move in progress (W1, W23, W29–W44 through the dom layer; W139 for tests).

exports.name: ResizeGesture
exports.description: A resize in progress (W6).

exports.name: ApplyLayoutResult
exports.description: What `applyLayout` did: windows it matched, and saved ids it found no open window for.

exports.name: WindowManager
exports.description: The manager.

exports.name: SNAPSHOT_VALUE_FIELDS
exports.description: Every `WindowSnapshot` field but `frame`; the manager test pins this list to the snapshot's keys, so a new field cannot be forgotten.

exports.name: BASE_STYLE
exports.description:
The base rules. Drag regions and grips take `touch-action: none` so a finger
drags the window instead of panning the page (W103), and never select text;
grips disappear where the core refuses a resize (maximised, fullscreen,
minimised, collapsed via the frame height, or not resizable).

exports.name: createGrips
exports.description: Appends the eight grips to `windowEl`; returns their removal.

exports.name: ensureBaseStyle
exports.description: Injects `BASE_STYLE` once into the document head or the shadow root that holds `el`.

exports.name: gripBand
exports.description: The grip band for the current primary pointer (W7, W106). Read when a window mounts.

exports.name: gripStyle
exports.description:
Inline placement of one grip inside the window box: `band` px thick, corners
`CORNER_GRIP_FACTOR` bands long. The top edge and the top corners stay at the
fine band whatever the pointer: the title bar lives there, and a coarse band
would turn a finger on the title (a move) into a resize from the top (found
by the touch check in `task windows:drag`). Top corners are long and thin for
the same reason, so the title bar's buttons stay pressable.

exports.name: desktopBounds
exports.description: The desktop's bounds in its own coordinates (W46): its padding box, origin at the top-left.

exports.name: measureDesktop
exports.description: Reads the desktop's frame: one `getBoundingClientRect` plus cached box metrics.

exports.name: toDesktopPoint
exports.description: A client point in desktop coordinates.
exports.signature: (frame: DesktopFrame, clientX: number, clientY: number) => Point

exports.name: DesktopFrame
exports.description: Everything needed to convert a client point, read once per gesture.

exports.name: attachDesktop
exports.description:
Binds `manager` to `desktop` (W136). The desktop element is the positioning
context: give it `position: relative` (or any non-static position) and a
size; windows are absolutely positioned inside it in its unscaled pixels.
exports.signature: <TData>(manager: WindowManager<TData>, desktop: HTMLElement, options?: AttachDesktopOptions) => DesktopBinding

exports.name: MODIFIER_KEYS
exports.description: Keyboard modifiers a gesture option can name.

exports.name: WINDOW_ACTIVATION
exports.description:
Click-vs-move thresholds (W5): the dnd kit's mouse and pen distance, so a
title-bar click and a list-row click feel the same. Touch uses a distance
too (the dnd kit's long-press is for rows that must still scroll): drag
regions are `touch-action: none`, so a finger on a title bar never pans.

exports.name: ActiveGestureInfo
exports.description: What `gesture()` reports while a pointer gesture runs.

exports.name: AttachDesktopOptions
exports.description: `attachDesktop` options; every one has a documented default.

exports.name: DesktopBinding
exports.description: The binding `attachDesktop` returns.

exports.name: GesturePointerKind
exports.description: The pointer kinds a window gesture can come from.

exports.name: ModifierKey
exports.description: A keyboard modifier, one of `MODIFIER_KEYS`.

exports.name: resolvePress
exports.description:
Classifies a press whose composed path is `path` (innermost first). `windows`
maps the mounted window elements to their ids; the first one on the path owns
the press, so a window nested in another window's content is its own.
`anywhere` = the move modifier is held (W3): any press in the window moves it,
except on a grip.
exports.signature: (path: readonly Element[], windows: ReadonlyMap<Element, string>, anywhere: boolean) => PressTarget | null

exports.name: WINDOW_INTERACTIVE_SELECTOR
exports.description:
Elements inside a drag region that keep their own press beyond the dnd kit's
interactive list: tabs in a title bar switch tabs, and the windows opt-out
marker. Combined with `INTERACTIVE_SELECTOR` through `pressHitsInteractive`.

exports.name: PressTarget
exports.description: The press, classified. `focus` = inside a window but not on a grip or a drag region.

exports.name: attachKeyboardModes
exports.description: Routes keys to `manager`'s keyboard mode while one runs; returns the detach.

exports.name: KEYBOARD_BIG_STEP_PX
exports.description: One Shift+arrow step, in desktop pixels.

exports.name: KEYBOARD_STEP_PX
exports.description: One arrow step, in desktop pixels; Shift takes `KEYBOARD_BIG_STEP_PX`.

exports.name: createLocalStorageLayoutStore
exports.description:
A `LayoutStore` over Web Storage. A value that is not valid JSON loads as
the raw string, so `parseLayout` reports it ("not an object") instead of the
store pretending nothing was saved. A storage that throws on access (a
private window, a blocked site) loads as nothing and rejects saves with the
browser's error.

exports.name: DEFAULT_LAYOUT_KEY_PREFIX
exports.description: Default key prefix: one namespace for every Kitora windows layout on the origin.

exports.name: LayoutStorage
exports.description: The part of Web Storage the store uses, so `sessionStorage`, a namespaced wrapper or a test double fits.

exports.name: LocalStorageLayoutStoreOptions
exports.description: Options for `createLocalStorageLayoutStore`.

exports.name: windowRegion
exports.description: A window's F6 region name (W98, the core's `KEYBOARD_REGION_ATTR`): `window-<id>`.

exports.name: WINDOW_ATTR
exports.description: On a window element: its window id. Written by `mount`; read by the hit test.

exports.name: TITLEBAR_ATTR
exports.description: On the title bar: a press here moves the window (W1).

exports.name: DRAG_REGION_ATTR
exports.description: Any other drag region inside a window: a toolbar, a frameless window's own area (W2, W124).

exports.name: NO_DRAG_ATTR
exports.description: Opt-out: a press inside an element carrying it never starts a move, whatever the element is (W4).

exports.name: EDGE_ATTR
exports.description: On a resize grip: its edge, one of `RESIZE_EDGES` (W6). The binding creates eight unless told not to.

exports.name: STATE_ATTR
exports.description: Mirrors the window's state (`normal`, `snapped`, …) so CSS can hide grips on a maximised window.

exports.name: FOCUSED_ATTR
exports.description: Present on the focused window (styling hook).

exports.name: RESIZABLE_ATTR
exports.description: `"false"` when the window cannot be resized: CSS hides its grips.

exports.name: GESTURE_ATTR
exports.description: On a window while a gesture runs: `move` or `resize`.

exports.name: SNAP_PREVIEW_ATTR
exports.description: The snap ghost the binding draws during a move (W37's plain form; the ui layer draws the styled one).

exports.name: SHIELD_ATTR
exports.description: The full-desktop shield laid over iframes during a gesture (W105).

exports.name: BASE_STYLE_ATTR
exports.description: Marks the binding's one injected `<style>` per document or shadow root.

exports.name: GESTURE_KINDS
exports.description: The gesture kinds a window can be in.

exports.name: GestureKind
exports.description: A gesture kind, one of `GESTURE_KINDS`.

exports.name: EDGE_CURSORS
exports.description: Resize cursor per grip (W16): the CSS bidirectional cursors, so the arrow matches the axis on every platform.

exports.name: FINE_GRIP_PX
exports.description:
Grip band on a fine pointer, in px (W7): eight times a 1 px border, the width
the OSes use for their invisible resize borders. The band lies INSIDE the
window box because `contain: paint` (W117) clips anything outside it.

exports.name: COARSE_GRIP_PX
exports.description: Grip band on a coarse pointer (W106): a fingertip is ~10 mm, so the band doubles.

exports.name: CORNER_GRIP_FACTOR
exports.description: A corner grip is this many bands long along each edge, so corners are easy to hit (W6).

exports.name: COARSE_POINTER_QUERY
exports.description: Media query that selects the coarse band.

exports.name: DOUBLE_CLICK_MS
exports.description: Two presses on a drag region within this many ms are a double-click (W22). The OS defaults sit at 400–500 ms.

exports.name: DOUBLE_CLICK_SLOP_PX
exports.description: …and within this many px of each other; further apart they are two separate clicks.

exports.name: SHIELD_Z
exports.description:
The z-index of the shield: above every window on the desktop (window z-indexes
are bounded to base + count, W64), so an iframe under the pointer never takes
the gesture's events.

exports.name: useIsomorphicLayoutEffect
exports.description: `useLayoutEffect` in the browser, `useEffect` on the server (no warning, nothing runs there).

exports.name: ContentEntry
exports.description: Imperatively opened content, kept by the provider until the window closes (W129–W131).

exports.name: WindowChrome
exports.description:
One chrome (W120–W125): how a window's frame looks. `className` goes on the
frame element the React layer owns (role, ref, the binding's attributes);
`render` draws everything inside it. The ui layer ships the presets; a host
writes its own from the headless parts (W123).

exports.name: WindowChromeProps
exports.description: The props a chrome renderer gets: the window, the id of its title element, and the content to wrap.

props.name: window
props.description: Snapshot of the window being drawn.

props.name: titleId
